verdict.rationale: GoDaddy documents an availability-check and search API, including a concrete v3 check-availability endpoint and a machine-readable OpenAPI spec, so code can call it directly; an official MCP server also exposes availability checks to agents. Rate limiting is documented only through a RateLimit-Remaining response header, and the evidence never states actual request quotas or window sizes, so the 'clear rate limits' part of the story is only partly covered. missing for 10: explicit published rate-limit numbers or windows for the check/search endpoints, independent or hands-on corroboration of the availability API.

support.subject: As a developer, I can check domain availability programmatically — a documented check/search API my code or agent can call with clear rate limits

citations.quote: Search operations let you check whether a specific domain is available for registration, and discover alternative names based on keywords or natural-language queries.
The `RateLimit-Remaining` header on every response shows how many requests remain in the current window.
The GoDaddy MCP server lets AI assistants search for domain names and check domain availability directly from a conversation
